correctness.rationale: For every fixed k>=2 and strictly positive a,b,lambda,mu, a two-state first-step Laplace-transform computation yields a killed shared active occupation with atom d and exponential rate r; conditioning leaf Poisson transmissions gives the exact NI beta-binomial mixture. In the LI model a killed two-state generator yields a two-exponential link survival nu(t); gamma-tail scaling of E[(1-nu(T))^k] proves the LI power exponent and prefactor. Small-time scaling proves its no-transmission probability is asymptotic to mu/(lambda*pi*k). A characteristic-polynomial argument shows rho<lambda*pi<lambda*mu/r, hence strict separation of exponents for all rates. Independent finite-state exact-rational absorption calculations verify both extremes at degrees 2,3,4,5 (unit rates), plus three non-symmetric positive parameter choices at degree 3, and direct quadrature corroborates k=20,100,500,2000 constants. See RESULT.md proof and check.py. No unproved passage from finite tests to infinite limits.

originality.rationale: The proposed novelty is not the generic Jensen or beta-binomial mixture, both established in earlier work. The new comparison is the shared-hub exponential switching law versus k independent identically switching edges, with exactly matched one-edge temporal processes, an NI zero-offspring atom, LI 1/k zero-offspring law, exact NI all-leaf beta/gamma probability and strict smaller NI than LI exponent for every positive parameter set. Moraes–Ferreira provides the motivation but not these exact claims; Giordano et al. gives fixed-time switched-Poisson count laws, while Hilton–Hall provides beta/zero-inflated epidemic offspring models without this switching comparison. The published research index exposes broader convex-order statements that cover only an ancillary observation. No covering exact atom-plus-two-exponent theorem identified; full access limits and historical priority remain risks.
residual_risks: Full source text for two closest published records could not be opened: only indexed claims available. Generic convex-order facts from these records are explicitly excluded from the novelty assertion.
Unindexed theoretical results on stopped Markov-modulated infection and contact clustering may already imply the exact pair of exponents.
The initiating paper switches all nodes, whereas the proved model switches only the infectious hub; the result does not imply whole-network epidemiological benefits.

value.rationale: The two infection mechanisms have identical complete one-edge temporal contact laws and equal reproduction mean, yet disagree in two operationally important rare outbreak extremes: the chance of no secondary infection remains positive under shared hub quarantine but vanishes like 1/k with independent link switching, while the chance of infecting every neighbor has a strictly lower power under shared quarantine. The exact nonzero atom and two provably distinct exponents are motivated hub superspreading/tail-risk quantities; they give a sharp boundary on any independently thinned-edge approximation. This is not just a numerical recalculation or unmotivated special slice. Limitations: fixed-rate one-source star SIR and Markovian stationary switching.
